query: Consider the following context: During the hot dip aluminum plating process, components such as sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates will come into long-term contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum and be corroded by the aluminum liquid, greatly reducing their service life. In that context, which material can be used for prepare parts for the dipping and plating equipment and protect the equipment from erosion, and why?

generation.hypothesis: High-entropy alloys with optimized composition for corrosion resistance can be used to prepare parts for the dipping and plating equipment, protecting the equipment from erosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy with a specific composition (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi) in a solid state
generation.intervention: Immersion in high-temperature liquid aluminum (around 700°C) for an extended period
generation.conditions: High-temperature environment, specifically the conditions present during the hot dip aluminum plating process
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective oxide layer on the surface of the high-entropy alloy
generation.mechanism: The alloying elements in the high-entropy alloy react with the oxygen in the environment to form a stable and dense oxide layer, which prevents the penetration of liquid aluminum and reduces corrosion
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in corrosion rate of at least 50% compared to conventional materials used in the hot dip aluminum plating process
generation.baseline: Conventional materials used in the hot dip aluminum plating process (e.g., steel or aluminum alloys)
generation.boundary: The high-entropy alloy must be able to withstand temperatures up to 800°C and maintain its corrosion resistance
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition of the high-entropy alloy and the optimal processing conditions for the alloy are still unknown and require further research

falsification_experiment.design: Immersion test of high-entropy alloy samples in high-temperature liquid aluminum, with regular measurements of corrosion rate and surface analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the corrosion rate of the high-entropy alloy is not reduced by at least 30% compared to the conventional material after 100 hours of immersion, the hypothesis is falsified
